heuristics.rule: CEC is the primary Express Entry pathway for PGWP holders already working in Canada
heuristics.condition: When an international student or worker is already in Canada with Canadian work experience
heuristics.action: Target the Canadian Experience Class (CEC) stream under Express Entry, not FSWP or FSTP
heuristics.because: CEC specifically rewards Canadian work experience, which PGWP holders accumulate; FSWP is designed for skilled workers outside Canada
heuristics.regulatory_basis: IRCC Express Entry — Canadian Experience Class program definition

heuristics.rule: PNP nomination adds +600 CRS points, effectively guaranteeing an ITA at the next draw
heuristics.condition: When a candidate's raw CRS score is below the general draw cutoff (typically 500+)
heuristics.action: Pursue a Provincial Nominee Program (PNP) nomination to add 600 points to CRS score
heuristics.because: PNP nomination adds 600 points, which exceeds all recent general draw cutoffs and makes selection virtually certain
heuristics.regulatory_basis: IRCC CRS additional points — Provincial Nominee Program nomination

heuristics.rule: BC PNP Tech stream can nominate eligible tech workers within 2 business days
heuristics.condition: When a tech worker holds an in-demand tech NOC code and has a job offer in BC
heuristics.action: Apply to BC PNP Tech stream as a priority pathway to the +600 CRS nomination
heuristics.because: BC PNP Tech stream specifically targets software, data, and IT management NOC codes and has a stated processing time of approximately 2 business days for nomination of in-demand codes

heuristics.rule: Candidate has exactly 60 days to submit full application after receiving an ITA
heuristics.condition: When IRCC issues an Invitation to Apply (ITA)
heuristics.action: Submit the complete permanent residence application within 60 days of ITA issuance
heuristics.because: The 60-day window is a hard deadline; failure to submit within this period results in the ITA expiring
heuristics.regulatory_basis: IRCC Express Entry — ITA submission deadline

heuristics.rule: Canadian PR holders must accumulate 730 days of physical presence in Canada per 5-year period to maintain PR status
heuristics.condition: When a Canadian PR holder resides outside Canada (e.g., returns to home country)
heuristics.action: Track and ensure at least 730 days of physical presence in Canada within every rolling 5-year period
heuristics.because: Failure to meet the 730-day residency obligation (2/5 rule) risks loss of PR status

heuristics.rule: Canadian citizenship eligibility requires 3 years of physical presence out of 5 years after obtaining PR
heuristics.condition: When a PR holder is planning for long-term immigration security or circular mobility
heuristics.action: Accumulate 3 years of physical presence in Canada within a 5-year window to become eligible for citizenship application
heuristics.because: Citizenship removes the residency obligation and provides permanent right to return regardless of time spent abroad
heuristics.regulatory_basis: IRCC — Canadian citizenship physical presence requirement

heuristics.rule: French language proficiency above CLB 7 in all areas adds +50 CRS points
heuristics.condition: When a candidate has French language skills above CLB 7 in all four language areas
heuristics.action: Submit qualifying French language test results (TEF/TCF) to claim additional 50 CRS points
heuristics.because: French language skills are an explicit additional-points category in CRS scoring and also unlock lower-cutoff French language proficiency draws
heuristics.regulatory_basis: IRCC CRS — additional points for French language skills

heuristics.rule: A job offer from a Canadian employer at NOC TEER 0 or 1 (senior management) adds +200 CRS points; other valid job offers add +50 points
heuristics.condition: When a candidate has a qualifying job offer from a Canadian employer
heuristics.action: Ensure the job offer is classified at NOC TEER 0/1 to claim the maximum +200 additional CRS points; otherwise claim +50
heuristics.because: The CRS point value of a job offer is directly tied to the NOC TEER classification of the offered position
heuristics.regulatory_basis: IRCC CRS — additional points for valid job offer

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines whether a candidate will receive an ITA in general or category-based draws; candidates below cutoff thresholds are not selected
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Without PNP: need typically 500+ for general draws; 470–510 for STEM category draws (2025 benchmarks). With PNP: +600 makes virtually any score competitive

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Age is a core human capital factor in CRS scoring; declining points after peak age window significantly reduces competitiveness
decision_factors.how_to_assess: CRS awards peak score for candidates aged 20–29; points decline significantly after age 45. Time-sensitive — delay in applying costs CRS points

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Each year of Canadian work experience (up to 5 years) adds significant CRS points under core human capital and skill transferability factors
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess current years of Canadian work experience; each additional year adds points up to the 5-year maximum

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines eligibility for category-based STEM draws, PNP Tech streams, and the point value of a job offer (TEER 0/1 vs. other)
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Verify whether occupation falls under targeted NOC codes (e.g., NOC 20012, NOC 21231, NOC 21232) for STEM draws and BC PNP Tech stream eligibility

decision_factors.why_it_matters: English/French language scores affect core human capital points and skill transferability points; CLB 9+ across all 4 bands maximizes points
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Use IELTS/CELPIP for English; TEF/TCF for French. Assess whether current scores reach CLB 9+ threshold for maximum points in all four language bands

decision_factors.why_it_matters: PNP nomination adds +600 CRS points, which is the single largest available point boost and effectively guarantees ITA selection
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess eligibility for province-specific streams (e.g., BC PNP Tech for tech workers with BC job offer; OINP Human Capital Priorities for Ontario candidates)

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Education is a core CRS human capital factor; PhD scores highest, bachelor's is baseline, no degree incurs significant penalty
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess highest completed credential; PhD maximizes education points, bachelor's degree is baseline reference

decision_factors.why_it_matters: If applicable, spouse/partner attributes (language, education, Canadian work experience) can add up to 40 additional CRS points
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Evaluate whether spouse/partner has qualifying language scores, education credentials, or Canadian work experience to contribute additional points

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Having a sibling who is a Canadian citizen or PR adds +15 CRS points
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Confirm whether a sibling holds Canadian citizenship or PR status

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Completing post-secondary education in Canada adds +30 CRS points (doctorate) or +15 points (secondary and above)
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Confirm whether the candidate completed eligible study in Canada at the appropriate level

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Criminal records or previous visa violations can significantly extend processing times beyond the 6-month service standard and may affect final decision
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Review applicant's history for criminal record, immigration violations, or other inadmissibility triggers before submitting application

decision_factors.why_it_matters: For Indian nationals, Canadian PR (~1–2 years) vs. US EB-2 (~134 years) represents a fundamentally different immigration security situation; for Chinese nationals, US EB-2 backlog is 5–10 years vs. Canadian PR ~1–2 years
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess current immigration status country, nationality-specific backlogs, and timeline to permanent status in each jurisdiction

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Accepting Canadian PR and staying in Canada long-term
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: CAD salaries for equivalent tech roles are typically 25–40% lower in USD terms than US equivalents; marginal tax rates of 40–49% on $150K+ income in BC and Ontario further reduce net take-home
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Tech workers and PMs comparing Canadian offers to US offers; those making stay-or-return financial calculations based on gross salary alone

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Returning to home country after obtaining Canadian PR
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: PR holder must maintain 730 days of physical presence in Canada per 5-year period or risk losing PR status; absence beyond this threshold triggers loss of PR without Canadian citizenship
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: PR holders who return to China or India for extended periods (e.g., 2–5 years) without yet having achieved citizenship

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Delaying Express Entry application to accumulate more Canadian work experience or improve CRS score
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Age is a core CRS human capital factor with peak scoring at ages 20–29 and significant decline after 45; delay directly reduces CRS points from the age factor
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Candidates in their late 30s or early 40s who defer application expecting to improve other CRS factors

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Relying solely on general Express Entry draws without pursuing PNP
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: General draw CRS cutoffs (481–524 in 2024) may be unachievable for many candidates without PNP; category-based draws (introduced 2023) offer lower cutoffs but require specific NOC code eligibility
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Candidates with mid-range CRS scores (450–490) who are not aware of PNP or category-based draw pathways

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Obtaining Canadian PR instead of pursuing US green card
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Canadian PR requires ongoing residency obligation (730 days per 5 years) to maintain status until citizenship; US LPR (green card) also requires US residency maintenance — but the circular mobility optionality of Canadian PR is greater once citizenship is obtained
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Candidates who assume PR status is unconditional and permanent from day one, without factoring in the residency obligation period before citizenship eligibility

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Targeting BC PNP Tech stream for +600 CRS points
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: BC PNP Tech stream requires a job offer in BC specifically; employer does not need to be BC-based but the worker's position must be in BC — candidates with job offers outside BC cannot use this stream
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Tech workers with job offers in Ontario or other provinces who assume BC PNP Tech is broadly available to all Canadian tech workers

failure_patterns.pattern: Failing to submit complete PR application within 60 days of ITA issuance
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: IRCC's ITA has a hard 60-day submission window; candidates who do not prepare documentation in advance may miss the deadline
failure_patterns.consequence: ITA expires; candidate returns to the pool and must wait for a new ITA in a future draw
warning_signs: Candidate has not pre-assembled supporting documents (language test results, ECA, employment records) before entering the pool
Candidate assumes ITA deadline is flexible or extendable

failure_patterns.pattern: PR holder loses status by failing to meet 730-day residency obligation
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Canadian PR requires 730 days of physical presence in Canada per 5-year period; extended return to home country without achieving citizenship risks falling below this threshold
warning_signs: PR holder returns to home country for more than 3 years within a 5-year period without obtaining citizenship
PR holder does not track days of physical presence in Canada

failure_patterns.pattern: Inadmissibility issues causing extended processing beyond service standard
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Criminal records or previous visa violations trigger additional review outside the standard 6-month processing pipeline
failure_patterns.consequence: Application processing extends significantly beyond the 6-month IRCC service standard; potential inadmissibility finding
warning_signs: Applicant has a prior criminal record in any country
Applicant has prior immigration violations or misrepresentation history

failure_patterns.pattern: CRS score below competitive threshold with no PNP or category-based draw pathway identified
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: General draw CRS cutoffs (481–524 in 2024) exclude candidates with mid-range scores who have not identified alternative pathways
failure_patterns.consequence: Candidate remains in the Express Entry pool indefinitely without receiving an ITA
warning_signs: Candidate's CRS score is below 480 without PNP nomination
Candidate's NOC code is not eligible for any category-based draw
Candidate has not assessed PNP stream eligibility

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the candidate have Canadian work experience, and if so, how many years?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines eligibility for the Canadian Experience Class (CEC) stream and the number of CRS points earned from Canadian work experience (up to 5 years)
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Confirm the NOC code of the Canadian work experience to assess CEC eligibility and category-based draw eligibility
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Candidate may need to rely on FSWP or FSTP; CEC pathway is unavailable

diagnostic_questions.question: What is the candidate's current CRS score, and does it meet the threshold for general draws (500+) or STEM category draws (470–510)?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines whether the candidate is currently competitive for an ITA without a PNP nomination
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Candidate may be competitive in the next general or category-based draw; monitor draw frequency and cutoffs
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Candidate should assess PNP eligibility to add +600 points or identify category-based draws with lower cutoffs

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the candidate eligible for a Provincial Nominee Program (PNP) stream, particularly the BC PNP Tech stream?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: PNP nomination adds +600 CRS points, which is the most decisive single factor in achieving Express Entry selection
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Pursue PNP nomination immediately; BC PNP Tech can nominate within 2 business days for in-demand tech NOC codes
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Assess other provincial streams (OINP, AAIP, MPNP) or focus on improving raw CRS score

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the candidate's NOC code fall under STEM occupation categories targeted by IRCC category-based draws (e.g., NOC 20012, 21231, 21232)?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines eligibility for STEM category-based draws, which have lower CRS cutoffs (481–510) than general draws
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Candidate should ensure profile is flagged for STEM category draws; lower cutoff may allow ITA without PNP
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Candidate must rely on general draws or other category draws (healthcare, trades, transport, French language)

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the candidate have strong French language skills above CLB 7 in all four language areas?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines eligibility for +50 additional CRS points and access to French language proficiency draws with significantly lower CRS cutoffs (400–450 range)
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Submit TEF/TCF scores; claim +50 CRS points and assess eligibility for French language draw pathway
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: French language draw pathway and +50 points are unavailable; focus on other CRS improvement strategies

diagnostic_questions.question: How old is the candidate, and are they approaching or past age 45?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Age is a core CRS human capital factor; significant point decline after 45 reduces competitiveness and creates time pressure to apply
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Urgency to apply increases; delay compounds CRS score loss from age factor
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Candidate retains full age-based CRS points; less urgency from age factor alone

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the candidate have a sibling who is a Canadian citizen or PR holder?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Sibling status adds +15 additional CRS points
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Claim +15 additional CRS points in Express Entry profile
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: No additional points available from this factor

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the candidate have any criminal record or history of visa violations or immigration misrepresentation?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Inadmissibility issues can extend processing times significantly beyond the 6-month service standard and may result in a denial
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Seek legal assessment of admissibility before submitting Express Entry profile; prepare for extended processing
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Standard processing timelines apply; no additional inadmissibility risk

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the candidate an Indian national currently on US H-1B status?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Reveals comparative immigration security context: Indian nationals face a ~134-year EB-2 backlog in the US vs. ~1–2 year Canadian PR timeline — a fundamentally different stay-or-return calculus
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Canadian Express Entry PR (~1–2 years) represents resolved immigration status vs. indefinite H-1B dependency; this changes the financial and personal planning calculus significantly
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Assess nationality-specific US backlog (e.g., EB-2 China: 5–10 years) to determine comparative urgency of Canadian PR pathway

industry_realities.common_belief: Express Entry is a visa or immigration status
industry_realities.actual_reality: Express Entry is a selection management system, not a visa. It is a mechanism through which candidates are invited to apply for permanent residence. Receiving an ITA is not the same as receiving PR.
industry_realities.implication: Candidates must understand that being in the Express Entry pool does not confer any immigration status; only a final positive PR decision grants permanent residence

industry_realities.common_belief: All nationalities face the same effective wait time for Canadian PR
industry_realities.actual_reality: CRS scoring requirements are the same for all nationalities, but the comparative value of Canadian PR differs significantly by nationality. For Indian nationals, the US EB-2 backlog is ~134 years vs. Canadian PR in ~1–2 years. For Chinese nationals, the US EB-2 backlog is 5–10 years vs. ~1–2 years for Canadian PR.
industry_realities.implication: Nationality-specific US backlog context should be a primary input in the stay-or-return decision; the immigration security differential is not uniform across nationalities

industry_realities.common_belief: Canadian PR is permanent and unconditional once granted
industry_realities.actual_reality: Canadian PR requires ongoing compliance with the 730-day physical presence residency obligation per 5-year period. PR status can be lost if this obligation is not met. Only Canadian citizenship is unconditional.
industry_realities.implication: PR holders planning extended returns to their home country must actively track and manage physical presence days or pursue citizenship (after 3 years) before extended absence

industry_realities.common_belief: You need to stay in Canada continuously after getting PR to maintain status
industry_realities.actual_reality: PR holders can live outside Canada for up to 3 out of 5 years (i.e., the 730-day minimum is met if the holder spends at least 2 out of every 5 years in Canada). Canadian citizenship, obtained after 3 years of presence, removes this constraint entirely.
industry_realities.implication: Canadian PR provides meaningful circular mobility — holders can return to home country for multi-year periods while maintaining PR, provided the 2/5 minimum is met

industry_realities.common_belief: IRCC processes all PR applications within 6 months
industry_realities.actual_reality: IRCC's service standard targets 6 months for 80% of complete applications. In 2024, IRCC reported approximately 82% of applications processed within 6 months. Applications with inadmissibility issues or requiring additional documentation take significantly longer.
industry_realities.implication: The 6-month timeline is a standard, not a guarantee; candidates with any inadmissibility history should plan for a longer timeline

industry_realities.common_belief: BC PNP Tech stream is available to any tech worker in Canada
industry_realities.actual_reality: BC PNP Tech stream requires the worker to have a job offer in BC. The employer does not need to be BC-based, but the worker's role must be in BC. Workers with job offers outside BC are not eligible for this stream.
industry_realities.implication: Tech workers in Ontario, Alberta, or other provinces must use their province's own PNP streams (e.g., OINP, AAIP) rather than BC PNP Tech, even if their NOC code would qualify

industry_realities.common_belief: A higher salary in Canada means equivalent or better financial outcomes vs. the US
industry_realities.actual_reality: CAD salaries for tech roles are typically 25–40% lower in USD terms than equivalent US roles. Marginal tax rates in BC (40–47%) and Ontario (43–49%) on $150K+ income further reduce net take-home. At CAD $150K in Toronto, after-tax take-home is approximately CAD $98,000–$105,000.
industry_realities.implication: Financial comparison between Canadian and US offers must be done on after-tax, USD-equivalent net income, not gross CAD figures; Canada's advantage is immigration security and universal healthcare, not higher net compensation

industry_realities.common_belief: Category-based draws were always part of Express Entry
industry_realities.actual_reality: Category-based draws were introduced in 2023. They target specific occupational and language categories (STEM, healthcare, trades, transport, French language) and often have lower CRS cutoffs than general draws.
industry_realities.implication: Candidates who have not updated their understanding of Express Entry since before 2023 may be unaware of category-based draw pathways that could make them eligible despite lower raw CRS scores

junior_vs_senior_signals.dimension: Understanding of Express Entry as a system vs. a visa
junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Treats Express Entry as equivalent to a visa or immigration status; believes entering the pool means immigration is in progress
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Understands Express Entry is a selection management system; distinguishes between pool entry, ITA receipt, application submission, and final PR decision as four distinct stages
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Conflating pool entry with PR approval leads to premature life decisions (e.g., quitting job, signing leases) before status is actually resolved

junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Focuses only on improving core human capital factors (language, education, work experience) and waits for a general draw
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Simultaneously assesses PNP eligibility for +600 points, category-based draw eligibility (STEM, French language), and job offer classification (TEER 0/1 for +200 vs. +50) as parallel pathways
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Relying solely on general draws with a sub-500 CRS score may mean indefinite pool residence; PNP or category-based draws are often the actual selection pathway

junior_vs_senior_signals.dimension: Evaluating Canadian PR value relative to nationality
junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Evaluates Canadian PR in isolation as 'good immigration status' without comparing it to the specific US green card backlog applicable to their nationality
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Calculates the precise comparative timeline: Indian national on H-1B faces ~134-year EB-2 wait vs. ~1–2 year Canadian PR — treats this as a fundamentally different security calculus; applies same comparative analysis for Chinese nationals (5–10 year US backlog)
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Nationality-specific backlog context is the most determinative factor in the stay-or-return immigration security analysis; generic 'PR is good' framing misses the differential entirely

junior_vs_senior_signals.dimension: Understanding PR residency obligation and circular mobility
junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Assumes Canadian PR is permanent and unconditional; does not track physical presence days; or conversely, assumes PR requires continuous residence in Canada
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Knows the 730-day per 5-year residency obligation precisely; understands circular mobility is possible (up to 3 years abroad) but citizenship (after 3 years presence) is the threshold for unconditional return rights
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Failure to track residency days risks loss of PR status; misunderstanding the rule in either direction leads to either unnecessary stays or inadvertent status loss

junior_vs_senior_signals.dimension: Financial comparison between Canadian and US compensation
junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Compares gross CAD salary to gross USD salary, or assumes similar purchasing power; concludes Canadian offers are competitive
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Converts to USD, applies 40–49% marginal tax rate on Canadian income above $150K, notes absence of health insurance costs as a partial offset, and concludes Canadian net compensation is materially lower than US equivalent — then factors in immigration security premium
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Overestimating Canadian net compensation leads to incorrect financial modeling for stay-or-return decisions; the correct frame is: Canada offers immigration security at a measurable net income discount

junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Enters Express Entry pool and begins document collection only after receiving ITA, assuming 60 days is sufficient time
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Pre-assembles all required documentation (ECA, language test results, employment records, police certificates) before or immediately after pool entry, so the 60-day ITA window is used for submission rather than collection
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Missing the 60-day ITA deadline causes the ITA to expire; candidate returns to pool and must wait for a new draw, potentially at a lower CRS score due to aging

junior_vs_senior_signals.dimension: BC PNP Tech stream eligibility assumption
junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Assumes BC PNP Tech is available to any tech worker in Canada with a qualifying NOC code
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Knows BC PNP Tech requires a job offer specifically in BC; workers with offers outside BC must use province-specific streams (OINP, AAIP, etc.) and cannot substitute BC PNP Tech
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Applying to an ineligible stream wastes time and delays PNP nomination; the +600 CRS pathway is province-specific and job-location-dependent
